question.problem:
Given the function $f(x;w)={w}_{1}{x}_{1}-{w}_{2}{x}_{2}+{w}_{3}{x}_{3},$ compute ${∇}_{w}\,f$ with the input $x={[\begin{aligned}-1,\,-2,\,4\end{aligned}]}^{T}.$
${∇}_{w}\,f=\text{ }$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
{{field-3}}
question.worked_solution:
To compute ${∇}_{w}\,f$, we take partial derivatives with respect to each component of $w.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{1}}({w}_{1}{x}_{1}-{w}_{2}{x}_{2}+{w}_{3}{x}_{3})={x}_{1} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{2}}({w}_{1}{x}_{1}-{w}_{2}{x}_{2}+{w}_{3}{x}_{3})=-{x}_{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂{w}_{3}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{w}_{3}}({w}_{1}{x}_{1}-{w}_{2}{x}_{2}+{w}_{3}{x}_{3})={x}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, with $x={[\begin{aligned}-1,\,-2,\,4\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{w}\,f & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
